Let $N_{\mathbb R}$ be the canonical positive real image of $|G|$ from [[def-qa-normalized-finite-abelian-fourier-transform]]. Define the finite coefficient matrix $U$, with rows indexed by $\widehat G$ and columns by $G$, by
$$U_{\chi,x}=N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\overline{\chi(x)},\qquad \chi\in\widehat G,\ x\in G.$$
It is square and satisfies $U^*U=I_G$ and $UU^*=I_{\widehat G}$, where $U^*$ is the conjugate transpose and $I_X$ is the identity matrix indexed by $X$, with $(I_X)_{x,y}=1$ when $x=y$ and $0$ otherwise. These two identities are the meaning of “unitary” here.

For $f\in\mathbb C^G$, define $F_Gf\in\mathbb C^{\widehat G}$ by $$ (F_Gf)(\chi):=N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in G}f(x)\overline{\chi(x)},\qquad \chi\in\widehat G. $$ Here $\mathbb C^X$ is the space of all functions $X\to\mathbb C$ ([[def-function-space]]) and the sum is the finite sum in $\mathbb C$ ([[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]]). This fixes the negative-character sign and uses the same factor $N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}$ in both directions. Unitarity is proved separately; it is not part of this definition.

derivations.claim: Write $F_Gf=Uf$ in the point-mass coordinate bases. From [F1], $U^*$ is a two-sided inverse of $U$, so $f=U^*(F_Gf)$.

The $x$ coordinate of $U^*(F_Gf)$ is $\sum_{\chi\in\widehat G}\overline{U_{\chi,x}}(F_Gf)(\chi)$. By [F2], $\overline{U_{\chi,x}}=N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\chi(x)$, which gives exactly the displayed formula.

For $C_2\times C_3$ and $C_2\times C_2$, apply the inverse product-character map [F9] to the cyclic characters: it gives the displayed formulas $\chi_{a,b}(u,v)=(-1)^{au}\omega^{bv}$ and $\chi_{a,b}(u,v)=(-1)^{au+bv}$. Their rows are distinct, since values at $(1,0)$ distinguish $a$, while values at $(0,1)$ distinguish $b$. The product-character bijection and cardinalities in [F9] show that the six and four displayed rows are complete.

Every entry of each table has modulus one by [F12]. For $C_2,C_3,C_4$, the row sum for labels $k,k'$ is $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\omega_n^{(k-k')j}$, and the column sum for labels $j,j'$ is $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\omega_n^{k(j-j')}$. In each case the sum is $n$ when the labels agree modulo $n$. Otherwise $q:=\omega_n^{k-k'}$ (or $\omega_n^{j-j'}$) is not $1$, has $q^n=1$, and $(1-q)\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}q^r=1-q^n=0$; cancellation in the field [F13] gives zero. This proves both orthogonality directions for the three cyclic tables, including the explicit $C_2$ and $C_3$ entries.

On $C_2\times C_2$, both orthogonality sums factor into two $C_2$ sums from step 1.2, so they equal $4$ for equal labels and $0$ otherwise. On $C_2\times C_3$, each row and column sum factors into its $C_2$ and $C_3$ cyclic sums from step 1.2, so they equal $6$ for equal labels and $0$ otherwise. Thus all five tables have orthogonal rows and orthogonal columns, with squared row and column norm equal to the group order.
